claim: DNA methyltransferase 3bb.1 (dnmt3bb.1) is essential for maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) fate as part of an early Notch-runx1-cmyb HSPC specification pathway in the zebrafish.
source: Here, we show that DNA methyltransferase 3bb.1 (dnmt3bb.1) is essential for maintenance of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) fate as part of an early Notch-runx1-cmyb HSPC specification pathway in the zebrafish.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by multiple experimental results throughout the manuscript including loss-of-function and gain-of-function studies.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1 is expressed in HSPC downstream from Notch1 and runx1.
source: Dnmt3bb.1 is expressed in HSPC downstream from Notch1 and runx1, and loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb locus methylation, reduced cmyb expression, and gradual reduction in HSPCs.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data showing dnmt3bb.1 expression is reduced in runx1 morphants and mind bomb mutants, and increased by runx1 overexpression.

claim: Loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb locus methylation.
source: Dnmt3bb.1 is expressed in HSPC downstream from Notch1 and runx1, and loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb locus methylation, reduced cmyb expression, and gradual reduction in HSPCs.
evidence: Supported by bisulfite sequencing data showing reduced methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.

claim: Loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb expression.
source: Dnmt3bb.1 is expressed in HSPC downstream from Notch1 and runx1, and loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb locus methylation, reduced cmyb expression, and gradual reduction in HSPCs.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data showing progressive loss of cmyb expression in dnmt3bb.1 mutants and morphants.

claim: Loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to gradual reduction in HSPCs.
source: Dnmt3bb.1 is expressed in HSPC downstream from Notch1 and runx1, and loss of Dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to reduced cmyb locus methylation, reduced cmyb expression, and gradual reduction in HSPCs.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization showing cmyb expression is present at 36 hpf but strongly reduced by 72 and 96 hpf in dnmt3bb.1 mutants.

claim: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to methylate the cmyb locus.
source: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to methylate the cmyb locus, promote cmyb expression, and promote hematopoietic development.
evidence: Supported by bisulfite sequencing showing methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected embryos.

claim: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to promote cmyb expression.
source: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to methylate the cmyb locus, promote cmyb expression, and promote hematopoietic development.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization showing cmyb expression in dnmt3bb.1-gfp expressing cells in early blastula embryos.

claim: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to promote hematopoietic development.
source: Ectopic overexpression of dnmt3bb.1 in non-hematopoietic cells is sufficient to methylate the cmyb locus, promote cmyb expression, and promote hematopoietic development.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization showing expression of hematopoietic lineage markers (rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, rag2, hbae1) in dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastula embryos.

claim: HSPCs arise during embryogenesis from hemogenic endothelial cells located in the ventral floor of the trunk dorsal aorta.
source: HSPCs arise during embryogenesis from hemogenic endothelial cells located in the ventral floor of the trunk dorsal aorta (Bertrand et al., 2010a; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Boisset et al., 2010; Murayama et al., 2006) that enter the circulation to seed hematopoietic organs and tissues and eventually give rise to all differentiated blood lineages (Bertrand et al., 2010a; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Murayama et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Hemogenic endothelial cells enter the circulation to seed hematopoietic organs and tissues and eventually give rise to all differentiated blood lineages.
source: HSPCs arise during embryogenesis from hemogenic endothelial cells located in the ventral floor of the trunk dorsal aorta (Bertrand et al., 2010a; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Boisset et al., 2010; Murayama et al., 2006) that enter the circulation to seed hematopoietic organs and tissues and eventually give rise to all differentiated blood lineages (Bertrand et al., 2010a; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Murayama et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The emergence of HSPCs from aortic endothelium is regulated by a Notch-Runx1-Cmyb signaling pathway.
source: The emergence of HSPCs from aortic endothelium is regulated by a Notch-Runx1-Cmyb signaling pathway (Burns et al., 2005; Clements et al., 2011; Richard et al., 2013; Bertrand et al., 2010b; Rowlinson and Gering, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Runx1 transcription factor is required downstream from Notch signaling and upstream from Cmyb for HSPC development from the endothelium.
source: Studies in mice and zebrafish have shown that the Runx1 transcription factor is required downstream from Notch signaling and upstream from Cmyb for HSPC development from the endothelium, although once HSPCs are specified, Runx1 transcription is down-regulated and it is not necessary for HSPC fate maintenance (Chen et al., 2009; Liakhovitskaia et al., 2009; Sood et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Tober et al., 2013; Lam et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies in mice and zebrafish.

claim: Once HSPCs are specified, Runx1 transcription is down-regulated and it is not necessary for HSPC fate maintenance.
source: Studies in mice and zebrafish have shown that the Runx1 transcription factor is required downstream from Notch signaling and upstream from Cmyb for HSPC development from the endothelium, although once HSPCs are specified, Runx1 transcription is down-regulated and it is not necessary for HSPC fate maintenance (Chen et al., 2009; Liakhovitskaia et al., 2009; Sood et al., 2010; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010; Tober et al., 2013; Lam et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cmyb is required for HSPC formation downstream from Runx1.
source: The transcription factor Cmyb is also required for HSPC formation downstream from Runx1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the hematopoietic pathway, supported by the context and citations in the manuscript.

claim: Cmyb expression persists in HSPC.
source: However, unlike Runx1, Cmyb expression persists in HSPC and its function is required not only for differentiation of HSPCs but also for their subsequent maintenance (Mukouyama et al., 1999; Mucenski et al., 1991; Soza-Ried et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cmyb function is required not only for differentiation of HSPCs but also for their subsequent maintenance.
source: However, unlike Runx1, Cmyb expression persists in HSPC and its function is required not only for differentiation of HSPCs but also for their subsequent maintenance (Mukouyama et al., 1999; Mucenski et al., 1991; Soza-Ried et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epigenetic regulatory mechanisms have been implicated in long-term maintenance of gene expression.
source: Epigenetic regulatory mechanisms have been implicated in long-term maintenance of gene expression (Deaton and Bird, 2011) and differentiated cell fate (Hu et al., 2012; Mohn et al., 2008; Lay et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2010), and we hypothesized that they might play a role in HSPC fate maintenance during the Runx1-independent phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epigenetic regulatory mechanisms have been implicated in maintenance of differentiated cell fate.
source: Epigenetic regulatory mechanisms have been implicated in long-term maintenance of gene expression (Deaton and Bird, 2011) and differentiated cell fate (Hu et al., 2012; Mohn et al., 2008; Lay et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2010), and we hypothesized that they might play a role in HSPC fate maintenance during the Runx1-independent phase.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) add a methyl group to the 5 position of cytosine residues in DNA, typically on cytosines in CpG dinucleotides.
source: In eukaryotes, DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) add a methyl group to the 5 position of cytosine residues in DNA, typically on cytosines in CpG dinucleotides.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNA methylation mechanisms.

claim: CpGs are often grouped in clusters called 'CpG islands' (CGIs), which are themselves frequently found within or in the 5' regions of genes.
source: CpGs are often grouped in clusters called 'CpG islands' (CGIs), which are themselves frequently found within or in the 5' regions of genes (Deaton and Bird, 2011; Suzuki and Bird, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about CpG islands, supported by citations.

claim: Mammalian DNMT1 acts as a maintenance enzyme and has high affinity for binding to hemimethylated DNA.
source: Mammalian DNMT1 acts as a maintenance enzyme and has high affinity for binding to hemimethylated DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNMT1 function.

claim: Mammalian DNMT3A and DNMT3B act as de novo methyltransferases and establish initial DNA methylation patterns.
source: Other mammalian DNMTs, including the DNMT3 family enzymes DNMT3A and DNMT3B, act as de novo methyltransferases and establish initial DNA methylation patterns (Goll and Bestor, 2005; Xu et al., 2010; Cheng and Blumenthal, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNMT3 family function, supported by citations.

claim: Genomic imprinting by DNA methylation has a well-documented role in reducing gene expression in both plants and animals.
source: Genomic imprinting by DNA methylation has a well-documented role in reducing gene expression in both plants and animals (Reik and Dean, 2001), for example, during X-chromosome inactivation in mammals (Tada et al., 2000; Gendrel and Heard, 2014) or repression of imprinted allele expression during Arabidopsis embryonic development (Jullien and Berger, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DNA methylation can act as a positive regulator for gene expression, particularly when methylation occurs in gene bodies as opposed to promoter or enhancer regions.
source: DNA methylation can also act as a positive regulator for gene expression, particularly when methylation occurs in gene bodies as opposed to promoter or enhancer regions (Baubec et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In mouse stem cells, DNMT3B selectively binds to and methylates gene body regions, excluding promoter and enhancer regions.
source: In mouse stem cells, DNMT3B selectively binds to and methylates gene body regions, excluding promoter and enhancer regions.
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Baubec et al., 2015.

claim: DNMT3B binding is found preferentially in gene body regions of actively expressed genes.
source: DNMT3B binding is found preferentially in gene body regions of actively expressed genes (Baubec et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Baubec et al., 2015.

claim: In the chick, DNMT3A acts as an epigenetic switch repressing neural and promoting neural crest fate by binding to and methylating the SOX2 and SOX3 promoters and inhibiting their expression.
source: In a recent elegant study performed in the chick, DNMT3A was shown to act as an epigenetic switch repressing neural and promoting neural crest fate by binding to and methylating the SOX2 and SOX3 promoters and inhibiting their expression (Hu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Hu et al., 2012.

claim: Around 36 hpf selected cells in the developing zebrafish dorsal aorta specifically express dnmt3bb.1.
source: Using whole-mount in situ (WISH) hybridization, we find that around 36 hpf selected cells in the developing zebrafish dorsal aorta specifically express DNA methyltransferase 3bb.1 (dnmt3bb.1)(Figure 1a,b), a gene most closely related to human DNMT3B (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1a,b.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is most closely related to human DNMT3B.
source: Using whole-mount in situ (WISH) hybridization, we find that around 36 hpf selected cells in the developing zebrafish dorsal aorta specifically express DNA methyltransferase 3bb.1 (dnmt3bb.1)(Figure 1a,b), a gene most closely related to human DNMT3B (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: DNMT3B functions as a de novo DNMT in humans, adding new methyl 'marks' to cytosine residues in DNA.
source: As noted above, DNMT3B functions as a de novo DNMT in humans, adding new methyl 'marks' to cytosine residues in DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about DNMT3B function.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1-positive cells are present in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta.
source: Dnmt3bb.1-positive cells are present in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta (Figure 1c,d) (Takayama et al., 2014; Thisse, 2001)), and double WISH confirms that dnmt3bb.1 is co-expressed with cmyb (Figure 1e,f), a known marker for developing HSPCs (Gering and Patient, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1c,d and citations.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is co-expressed with cmyb.
source: Dnmt3bb.1-positive cells are present in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta (Figure 1c,d) (Takayama et al., 2014; Thisse, 2001)), and double WISH confirms that dnmt3bb.1 is co-expressed with cmyb (Figure 1e,f), a known marker for developing HSPCs (Gering and Patient, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1e,f.

claim: cmyb is a known marker for developing HSPCs.
source: Dnmt3bb.1-positive cells are present in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta (Figure 1c,d) (Takayama et al., 2014; Thisse, 2001)), and double WISH confirms that dnmt3bb.1 is co-expressed with cmyb (Figure 1e,f), a known marker for developing HSPCs (Gering and Patient, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Gering and Patient, 2005.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is expressed specifically in HSPCs in the developing trunk.
source: dnmt3bb.1 is expressed specifically in HSPCs in the developing trunk, although expression is also present in portions of the eye and a few other selected head tissues during early development (Aanes et al., 2011) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and citation.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 expression is also present in portions of the eye and a few other selected head tissues during early development.
source: dnmt3bb.1 is expressed specifically in HSPCs in the developing trunk, although expression is also present in portions of the eye and a few other selected head tissues during early development (Aanes et al., 2011) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–e and citation.

claim: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in runx1 morpholino-injected animals.
source: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in runx1 morpholino-injected animals or runx1W84X mutants (Sood et al., 2010) (Figure 1h,i,m), while over-expression of runx1 by injection of runx1 mRNA results in increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in the axial vasculature (Figure 1i,j,m).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1h,i,m.

claim: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in runx1W84X mutants.
source: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in runx1 morpholino-injected animals or runx1W84X mutants (Sood et al., 2010) (Figure 1h,i,m), while over-expression of runx1 by injection of runx1 mRNA results in increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in the axial vasculature (Figure 1i,j,m).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1h,i,m and citation.

claim: Over-expression of runx1 by injection of runx1 mRNA results in increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in the axial vasculature.
source: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in runx1 morpholino-injected animals or runx1W84X mutants (Sood et al., 2010) (Figure 1h,i,m), while over-expression of runx1 by injection of runx1 mRNA results in increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in the axial vasculature (Figure 1i,j,m).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1i,j,m.

claim: Expression of dnmt3bb.1 is strongly reduced in Notch-deficient mindbomb (mib) mutants.
source: Similarly, expression of dnmt3bb.1 is also strongly reduced in Notch-deficient mindbomb (mib) mutants (Figure 1k,l,m).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1k,l,m.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification.
source: These results show that dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification (Burns et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2009; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), and that its expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing dnmt3bb.1 expression is regulated by Notch and Runx1, combined with citations to previous studies.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
source: These results show that dnmt3bb.1 is expressed by developing HSPCs downstream from the established Notch-Runx1 pathway for HSPC specification (Burns et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2009; Kissa and Herbomel, 2010), and that its expression is lost when HSPCs are not properly specified.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that dnmt3bb.1 expression is reduced in runx1 and mib mutants where HSPCs are not properly specified.

claim: A dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant allele encodes a polypeptide prematurely truncated at amino acid 172 (P166fs) due to an 11 nucleotide deletion.
source: We obtained a dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant allele encoding a polypeptide prematurely truncated at amino acid 172 (P166fs) due to an 11 nucleotide deletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular characterization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–e.

claim: Two to five dpf dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants are morphologically indistinguishable from their wild-type siblings.
source: Morphologically, two to five dpf dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants are indistinguishable from their wild-type siblings (Figure 2a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmitted light images shown in Figure 2a,b.

claim: At 36 hpf, cmyb expression in HSPCs in the ventral aorta is similar in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant embryos and their wild type siblings.
source: At 36 hpf, cmyb expression in HSPCs in the ventral aorta is similar in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutant embryos and their wild type siblings (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: By 72 and 96 hpf cmyb expression is strongly reduced in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
source: However, by 72 and 96 hpf cmyb expression is strongly reduced in the caudal hematopoietic tissue (CHT) of dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants (Figure 2e–h), as confirmed by genotyping of blindly scored embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2e–h and genotyping data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Loss of cmyb is accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin in the CHT at 72 hpf in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
source: Loss of cmyb is also accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin (Herbomel et al., 1999) in the CHT at 72 hpf (Figure 2i,j) and lymphoid marker rag1 (Willett et al., 1997) in the 5 dpf thymus (Figure 2k,l).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2i,j and citation.

claim: Loss of cmyb is accompanied by strong reduction in lymphoid marker rag1 in the 5 dpf thymus in dnmt3bb.1y258 mutants.
source: Loss of cmyb is also accompanied by strong reduction in myeloid marker l-plastin (Herbomel et al., 1999) in the CHT at 72 hpf (Figure 2i,j) and lymphoid marker rag1 (Willett et al., 1997) in the 5 dpf thymus (Figure 2k,l).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2k,l and citation.

claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show progressive loss of cmyb expression.
source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f.

claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of l-plastin in the 72 hpf CHT.
source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i.

claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of erythroid marker gata1 in the 72 hpf CHT.
source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n.

claim: Wild type embryos injected with dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos show reduced expression of rag1, ikaros, and lck:gfp in the 5 dpf thymus.
source: We observed similar hematopoietic defects in wild type embryos injected with any one of three different dnmt3bb.1-targeting morpholinos, with progressive loss of cmyb expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 2a–f) as well as reduced expression of l-plastin (Figure 2—figure supplement 2g,i) and erythroid marker gata1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2k–n) in the 72 hpf CHT, and reduced expression of rag1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j), ikaros, and lck:gfp (Figure 2—figure supplement 2o–r) in the 5 dpf thymus.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2h,j,o–r.

claim: Quantitative RT-PCR confirmed progressive loss of cmyb and strong reduction in subsequent l-plastin and rag1 expression in Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR confirmed progressive loss of cmyb and strong reduction in subsequent l-plastin and rag1 expression in Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals (Figure 2m,n).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2m,n.

claim: Strong increase in active caspase 3 in HSPC in the trunks of 48 hpf Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals indicated that HSPCs are undergoing apoptosis.
source: Strong increase in active caspase 3 in HSPC in the trunks of 48 hpf Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals indicated that HSPCs are undergoing apoptosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a–c).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical staining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3a–c.

claim: Despite dramatic hematopoietic defects, Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals appeared otherwise unaffected, with normal vascular patterning and vascular gene expression.
source: Despite dramatic hematopoietic defects, Dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals appeared otherwise unaffected, with normal vascular patterning and vascular gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 3d–i).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmitted light images, confocal images, and in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3d–i.

claim: Loss of dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to a specific defect in HSPCs, with progressive loss of cmyb expression and decreased numbers of HSPCs.
source: These results suggest that loss of dnmt3bb.1 activity leads to a specific defect in HSPCs, with progressive loss of cmyb expression and decreased numbers of HSPCs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion inferred from the multiple experimental results showing HSPC-specific defects in dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.

claim: RNAseq analysis showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
source: RNAseq analysis (and subsequent qPCR validation of selected genes) showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs, while many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased relative to control HSPCs (Figure 3b,c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs relative to control HSPCs.
source: RNAseq analysis (and subsequent qPCR validation of selected genes) showed that the expression of a variety of hematopoietic genes was reduced in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs, while many endothelial and apoptosis pathway genes were increased relative to control HSPCs (Figure 3b,c, Figure 3—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Figure 3b,c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Ingenuity pathway analysis confirmed elevated VEGF/angiogenesis and apoptosis pathway gene expression indicating lack of endothelial to hematopoietic transition and induction of apoptosis in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
source: Ingenuity pathway analysis (www.qiagen.com/ingenuity) confirmed elevated VEGF/angiogenesis and apoptosis pathway gene expression indicating lack of endothelial to hematopoietic transition and induction of apoptosis in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by Ingenuity pathway analysis results shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Very few of the hematopoietic or endothelial genes with significantly altered expression displayed significantly decreased DNA methylation in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
source: However, RRBS analysis revealed that very few of the hematopoietic or endothelial genes with significantly altered expression displayed significantly decreased DNA methylation (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RRBS analysis results.

claim: cmyb was one of the most affected and highly correlated of the hematopoietic genes that showed both significantly reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs and significantly reduced methylation of an adjacent promoter or gene body CpG island.
source: cmyb was one of the most affected and highly correlated of the hematopoietic genes that showed both significantly reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs and significantly reduced methylation of an adjacent promoter or gene body CpG island (Figure 3e, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by combined RRBS and RNAseq analysis shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: There was no change in methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.
source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3g.

claim: There was no change in methylation of CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC.
source: Direct sequencing of PCR-amplified fragments from bisulfite treated DNA confirmed reduced methylation in the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs (Figure 3f), but no change in the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 3g), or in CpG islands from a number of other hematopoietic and endothelial genes showing significantly altered expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC (Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: cmyb is a target of dnmt3bb.1-mediated regulation in HSPCs.
source: These results suggest that cmyb is a target of dnmt3bb.1-mediated regulation in HSPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined RRBS and RNAseq data showing cmyb has both reduced methylation and reduced expression in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPCs.

claim: 319 genes were identified whose expression in blood had been confirmed by in situ staining or PCR.
source: Genes expressed by blood cells were identified in the ZFIN zebrafish gene expression database (http://zfin.org/cgi-bin/webdriver?MIval=aa-ZDB_home.apg) using search terms blood, HSCs, ventral wall of dorsal aorta, and all associated search terms. 319 genes were identified whose expression in blood had been confirmed by in situ staining or PCR.
evidence: This claim is based on a database search and analysis described in the methods.

claim: 57 of the 319 hematopoietic genes were found to have a total of 72 CpG islands in their gene bodies.
source: Each of these 319 gene loci were then further analyzed using the UCSC genome browser or WashU epigenetics browser to determine whether there were CpG islands in their gene bodies. The gene body was defined as 5'UTR, all exons and introns and 3' UTR. 57 genes with 72 CpG islands in their gene bodies were identified.
evidence: This claim is based on computational analysis of gene structures.

claim: 10 of the 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells.
source: We carried out bisulfite restriction analysis to determine whether these 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells, using genomic DNA isolated from circulating blood cells obtained after amputating the tails of 5–7-day-old zebrafish (Figure 4a), and determined that 10 of the 72 CpG islands are methylated in blood cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite restriction analysis described in the text and Figure 4a.

claim: Only the cmyb intron 1 CpG island showed dnmt3bb.1-dependent changes in methylation among the 10 methylated CpG islands.
source: To determine whether methylation of these CpG islands was dnmt3bb.1-dependent, we carried out bisulfite sequencing on each of the 10 methylated CpG islands using 5 dpf blood cell genomic DNA isolated from either control or dnmt3bb.1 morpholino-injected zebrafish. Only one CpG island showed dnmt3bb.1-dependent changes in methylation, the cmyb intron 1 CpG island (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island in dnmt3bb.1-deficient blood cells.
source: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 4c), or in any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells (Figure 4d–k).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: No change was detected in the methylation of any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells in dnmt3bb.1-deficient animals.
source: No change was detected in the methylation of the runx1 exon 3 CpG island (Figure 4c), or in any of the other eight hematopoietic genes containing methylated CpG islands in blood cells (Figure 4d–k).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 4d–k.

claim: cmyb is a key proximal hematopoietic target of dnmt3bb.1.
source: These results support the findings of our RRBS analysis above, suggesting that cmyb is a key proximal hematopoietic target of dnmt3bb.1.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the genome-wide screen showing only cmyb CpG island methylation is dnmt3bb.1-dependent.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive in Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals.
source: In Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive, and double–positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk (Figure 5b,c,d), but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature (Figure 5b,e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5b,c,d,e,f.

claim: Double-positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk, but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature in Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals.
source: In Tol2(kdrl:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected animals Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-positive cells were consistently also cmyb positive, and double–positive cells were found throughout the vasculature, not only in their normal location in the trunk (Figure 5b,c,d), but also in ectopic locations such as the cranial vasculature (Figure 5b,e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 5b,c,d,e,f.

claim: Forced expression of dnmt3bb.1 can promote cmyb expression in endothelial cells even in the absence of runx1 function.
source: We observed similar induction of cmyb expression in dnmt3bb.1-gfp expressing cells when the transgene was injected into runx1 mutant animals lacking endogenous cmyb expression in HSPCs (Figure 5b,g,h), showing that the forced expression of dnmt3bb.1 can promote cmyb expression in endothelial cells even in the absence of runx1 function.
evidence: This claim is supported by double in situ hybridization data in runx1 mutants shown in Figure 5b,g,h.

claim: Heat shocked animals expressing Dnmt3bb.1-GFP fusion protein from the injected Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene showed robust mosaic expression of cmyb, rag1, and l-plastin.
source: In contrast, heat shocked animals expressing Dnmt3bb.1-GFP fusion protein from the injected Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene showed robust mosaic expression of cmyb, rag1, and l-plastin (Figure 6f-h,k).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6f-h,k.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells.
source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells (Jin et al., 2009), showing induction of erythroid lineage genes also occurs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h), but they do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h and citation.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2).
source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP-injected embryos also express lymphoid markers ikaros and rag2, as well as hemoglobin ae1 (hbae1), a marker of both primitive and definitive erythroid cells (Jin et al., 2009), showing induction of erythroid lineage genes also occurs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h), but they do not express endothelial markers cadherin 5 (cdh5) and ets-related protein (etsrp, also known as etv2) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1i–l.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 specifically promotes hematopoietic development without inducing mesoderm, endothelial precursors, or 'hemangioblasts'.
source: This suggests that dnmt3bb.1 specifically promotes hematopoietic development without inducing mesoderm, endothelial precursors, or 'hemangioblasts'.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that dnmt3bb.1 overexpression induces hematopoietic markers but not endothelial markers.

claim: 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells homing to the thymus.
source: On day 5, 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells (red fluorescent, rhodamine/biotin-dextran-labeled) homing to the thymus, as compared to only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat -shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors (Figure 6n–q).
evidence: This claim is supported by transplantation experiment data shown in Figure 6n–q.

claim: Only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors showed donor cells homing to the thymus.
source: On day 5, 17/30 (57%) of the host animals that received cells from heat shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) donors showed donor cells (red fluorescent, rhodamine/biotin-dextran-labeled) homing to the thymus, as compared to only 11/38 (29%) of host animals that received cells from control heat -shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) donors (Figure 6n–q).
evidence: This claim is supported by transplantation experiment data shown in Figure 6n–q.

claim: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts.
source: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts, while the number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitation of transplanted cells shown in Figure 6q.

claim: The number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable between dnmt3bb.1-gfp and control gfp transplanted hosts.
source: The thymus-positive dnmt3bb.1-gfp transplanted hosts had approximately twice as many cells in the thymus compared to the thymus-positive gfp control transplanted hosts, while the number of intravenously injected cells that were lodged non-specifically in the heart and aortic arches was comparable.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitation of transplanted cells shown in Figure 6q.

claim: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat-shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals.
source: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat -shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals, but not in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals (Figure 7a).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: The cmyb intron 1 CpG island does not become methylated in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals.
source: Bisulfite sequencing reveals that the cmyb intron 1 CpG island becomes methylated in DNA from heat -shocked mosaic Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals, but not in DNA from heat shocked control Tol2(hsp70:gfp) transgene-injected animals (Figure 7a).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: A separate cmyb 5' CpG island that is not normally methylated in HSPC in wild type animals does not become ectopically methylated in heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals.
source: A separate cmyb 5' CpG island that is not normally methylated in HSPC in wild type animals does not become ectopically methylated in heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected shield stage animals (Figure 7b).
evidence: This claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Chromatin immunoprecipitation shows that dnmt3bb.1-GFP binds to two independent DNA sequences from the cmyb intron 1 CpG island.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) of DNA from heat-shocked Tol2(hsp70:gfp) or Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene-injected or Tg(hsp70:tcf-gfp) germline transgenic (Lewis et al., 2004) shield-stage animals (Figure 7c) using anti-GFP antibodies shows that dnmt3bb.1-GFP (but not Tcf-GFP) binds to two independent DNA sequences from the cmyb intron 1 CpG island (Figure 7d, rows 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, rows 1 and 2.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP does not bind to non-CpG island cmyb DNA from intron 1 or exon 5, or to CpG island DNA from the runx1 or ntla gene loci.
source: Dnmt3bb.1-GFP does not bind to non-CpG island cmyb DNA from intron 1 or exon 5, or to CpG island DNA from the runx1 or ntla gene loci (Figure 7d, rows 3–6).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, rows 3–6.

claim: Tcf-GFP shows specific association with sox3 DNA sequences containing known TCF binding sites.
source: As an additional ChIP control, Tcf-GFP (but not Dnmt3bb.1-gfp) shows specific association with sox3 DNA sequences containing known TCF binding sites (Lee et al., 2006) (Figure 7d, row 7), but does not associate with any dnmt3bb.1 DNA sequence.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7d, row 7 and citation.

claim: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone.
source: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine (Figure 7e) confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone (Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2), as well as 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands (Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2.

claim: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine shows 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands.
source: ChIP using anti-methyl cytosine (Figure 7e) confirms methylation of the cmyb intron 1 CpG island in animals expressing dnmt3bb.1-GFP but not GFP alone (Figure 7e, rows 1 and 2), as well as 'constitutive' methylation of the runx1 and ntla CpG islands (Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 7e, rows 5 and 6.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs.
source: Together, these results suggest that Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs, and that loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined bisulfite sequencing and ChIP data showing dnmt3bb.1 binds to and methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island.

claim: Loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
source: Together, these results suggest that Dnmt3bb.1 methylates the cmyb intron 1 CpG island to maintain the expression of cmyb in HSPCs, and that loss of Dnmt3bb.1 results in failure to maintain cmyb expression and loss of HSPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the combined loss-of-function and molecular data.

claim: 10–12% of homozygous dnmt3bb.1 mutants survive to adulthood.
source: In a similar fashion, we find that 10–12% of homozygous dnmt3bb.1 mutants also survive to adulthood (Figure 8a,b), and the anterior kidneys in these surviving mutants also exhibit severely reduced hematopoietic cellularity (Figure 8c–f).
evidence: This claim is supported by observation of adult mutants shown in Figure 8a,b.

claim: The anterior kidneys in surviving adult dnmt3bb.1 mutants exhibit severely reduced hematopoietic cellularity.
source: In a similar fashion, we find that 10–12% of homozygous dnmt3bb.1 mutants also survive to adulthood (Figure 8a,b), and the anterior kidneys in these surviving mutants also exhibit severely reduced hematopoietic cellularity (Figure 8c–f).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 8c–f.

claim: The circulating erythrocytes that are present in adult dnmt3bb.1 mutants are mostly malformed.
source: The circulating erythrocytes that are present in adult mutants are mostly malformed (Figure 8g–i).
evidence: This claim is supported by blood smear analysis shown in Figure 8g–i.

claim: Sorted HSPCs from dnmt3bb.1-deficient 48 hpf embryos display malformations including abnormally shaped, bi-lobed or even multiple distinct nuclei.
source: Interestingly, sorted HSPCs from dnmt3bb.1-deficient 48 hpf embryos also display malformations including abnormally shaped, bi-lobed or even multiple distinct nuclei (Figure 8j,k).
evidence: This claim is supported by Giemsa staining of sorted HSPCs shown in Figure 8j,k.

claim: These results are similar to findings with cmyb mutants.
source: Again, these results are similar to findings with cmyb mutants (Soza-Ried et al., 2010), supporting the idea that Dnmt3bb.1 exerts its effects on HSPC fate maintenance and hematopoietic gene expression via Cmyb.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison to published cmyb mutant phenotypes.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1 exerts its effects on HSPC fate maintenance and hematopoietic gene expression via Cmyb.
source: Again, these results are similar to findings with cmyb mutants (Soza-Ried et al., 2010), supporting the idea that Dnmt3bb.1 exerts its effects on HSPC fate maintenance and hematopoietic gene expression via Cmyb.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the similarity of dnmt3bb.1 and cmyb mutant phenotypes.

claim: Heat shock induction of embryos injected with Tol2(hsp70:cmyb-2A-mCherry) leads to ectopic expression of hbae1, rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, lck and rag2.
source: Like overexpression of dnmt3bb.1-gfp in early embryos, heat shock induction of embryos injected with Tol2(hsp70:cmyb-2A-mCherry) leads to ectopic expression of hbae1, rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, lck and rag2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1b–m), but not endothelial markers cdh5 or etsrp (Figure 8—figure supplement 1n–q).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1b–m.

claim: Heat shock induction of embryos injected with Tol2(hsp70:cmyb-2A-mCherry) does not lead to expression of endothelial markers cdh5 or etsrp.
source: Like overexpression of dnmt3bb.1-gfp in early embryos, heat shock induction of embryos injected with Tol2(hsp70:cmyb-2A-mCherry) leads to ectopic expression of hbae1, rag1, l-plastin, ikaros, lck and rag2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1b–m), but not endothelial markers cdh5 or etsrp (Figure 8—figure supplement 1n–q).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1n–q.

claim: Co-injection of the Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene together with cmyb morpholino results in dramatic reduction in l-plastin and rag1 in dnmt3bb.1-GFP over-expressing embryos.
source: To more directly examine whether cmyb is required downstream from dnmt3bb.1 for induction of hematopoietic lineage genes, we co-injected the Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene together with a previously published cmyb morpholino(Grabher et al., 2011) and heat shocked as described above. We saw dramatic reduction in l-plastin and rag1 in dnmt3bb.1-GFP over-expressing embryos co-injected with cmyb morpholino compared to embryos injected with Tol2(hsp70:dnmt3bb.1-gfp) transgene alone (Figure 6g,h,i,j).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6g,h,i,j and citation.

claim: cmyb function is both necessary and sufficient for the expression of hematopoietic lineage genes.
source: Together, these results confirm that cmyb function is both necessary and sufficient for the expression of hematopoietic lineage genes, and further shows that the expression of hematopoietic genes cannot be induced by dnmt3bb.1 in the absence of cmyb.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the cmyb overexpression and knockdown experiments.

claim: The expression of hematopoietic genes cannot be induced by dnmt3bb.1 in the absence of cmyb.
source: Together, these results confirm that cmyb function is both necessary and sufficient for the expression of hematopoietic lineage genes, and further shows that the expression of hematopoietic genes cannot be induced by dnmt3bb.1 in the absence of cmyb.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that dnmt3bb.1-induced hematopoietic gene expression is blocked by cmyb knockdown.

claim: cmyb is a key locus regulated by dnmt3bb.1 during hematopoietic differentiation.
source: This suggests that cmyb is a key locus regulated by dnmt3bb.1 during hematopoietic differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from all the experimental data showing cmyb is a target of dnmt3bb.1 and is required for dnmt3bb.1-mediated hematopoietic gene expression.

claim: An epigenetic regulatory factor promotes the maintenance of hematopoietic cell fate downstream from an established genetic pathway required for the specification of HSPCs.
source: In this manuscript, we show that an epigenetic regulatory factor promotes the maintenance of hemtopoietic cell fate downstream from an established genetic pathway required for the specification of HSPCs
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main finding, supported by all the experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The de novo DNA methyltransferase dnmt3bb.1, the closest zebrafish ortholog of the mammalian DNA methyltransferase DNMT3B, is expressed specifically in cmyb-positive HSPC emerging from hemogenic endothelium in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta.
source: The de novo DNA methyltransferase dnmt3bb.1, the closest zebrafish ortholog of the mammalian DNA methyltransferase DNMT3B, is expressed specifically in cmyb-positive HSPC emerging from hemogenic endotheium in the ventral floor of the dorsal aorta.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: HSPC specification is controlled by a genetically programmed Notch-Runx1-Cmyb pathway.
source: HSPC specification is controlled by a genetically programmed Notch-Runx1-Cmyb pathway (Burns et al., 2005; Gering and Patient, 2005; Bresciani et al., 2014; Duncan et al., 2005; Bertrand et al., 2010b; Kumano et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Runx1 mutants and runx1 morpholino-injected zebrafish display reduced expression of dnmt3bb.1.
source: Runx1 mutants and runx1 morpholino-injected zebrafish display reduced expression of dnmt3bb.1, as do Notch-deficient mind bomb mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data.

claim: Notch-deficient mind bomb mutants display reduced expression of dnmt3bb.1.
source: Runx1 mutants and runx1 morpholino-injected zebrafish display reduced expression of dnmt3bb.1, as do Notch-deficient mind bomb mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data.

claim: Reduced dnmt3bb.1 expression in runx1 and mind bomb mutant embryos may reflect reduced HSPC numbers rather than the loss of direct gene regulation.
source: Since runx1 and mind bomb mutant embryos have strongly reduced numbers of HSPCs, reduced dnmt3bb.1 expression may reflect reduced HSPC numbers rather than the loss of direct gene regulation.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism underlying reduced dnmt3bb.1 expression in mutants.

claim: Overexpression of runx1 leads to increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in hemogenic endothelium.
source: Conversely, overexpression of runx1 leads to increased expression of dnmt3bb.1 in hemogenic endothelium.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data.

claim: Mouse Dnmt3b is expressed by developing CD34+ HSPCs in the endothelium of early mouse embryos.
source: Since mouse Dnmt3b is also expressed by developing CD34+ HSPCs in the endothelium of early mouse embryos (Watanabe et al., 2004), and is up-regulated by Oct4 in direct conversion of fibroblasts into multi-potent blood progenitors in cell culture (Szabo et al., 2010), this suggests that the role of these orthologous DNMT proteins may be conserved during early hematopoietic development in vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Watanabe et al., 2004.

claim: Mouse Dnmt3b is up-regulated by Oct4 in direct conversion of fibroblasts into multi-potent blood progenitors in cell culture.
source: Since mouse Dnmt3b is also expressed by developing CD34+ HSPCs in the endothelium of early mouse embryos (Watanabe et al., 2004), and is up-regulated by Oct4 in direct conversion of fibroblasts into multi-potent blood progenitors in cell culture (Szabo et al., 2010), this suggests that the role of these orthologous DNMT proteins may be conserved during early hematopoietic development in vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Szabo et al., 2010.

claim: The role of orthologous DNMT proteins may be conserved during early hematopoietic development in vertebrates.
source: Since mouse Dnmt3b is also expressed by developing CD34+ HSPCs in the endothelium of early mouse embryos (Watanabe et al., 2004), and is up-regulated by Oct4 in direct conversion of fibroblasts into multi-potent blood progenitors in cell culture (Szabo et al., 2010), this suggests that the role of these orthologous DNMT proteins may be conserved during early hematopoietic development in vertebrates.
evidence: This is speculation based on the similarity of expression patterns between zebrafish and mouse.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is required for HSPC maintenance.
source: Our loss- and gain-of-function data show that dnmt3bb.1 is required for HSPC maintenance.
evidence: This claim is supported by loss-of-function and gain-of-function experimental data.

claim: In dnmt3bb.1 mutants or dnmt3bb.1 morpholino-injected animals HSPC are initially specified but subsequently undergo apoptosis with mutant embryos showing gradual reduction in cmyb+ HSPCs.
source: In dnmt3bb.1 mutants or dnmt3bb.1 morpholino-injected animals HSPC are initially specified but subsequently undergo apoptosis with mutant embryos showing gradual reduction in cmyb+ HSPCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and caspase3 staining data.

claim: Mutants and morphants show later defects in downstream blood lineages, as evidenced by the reduced expression of specific markers of the myeloid, lymphoid, and erythroid lineages.
source: Mutants and morphants also show later defects in downstream blood lineages, as evidenced by the reduced expression of specific markers of the myeloid, lymphoid, and erythroid lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data showing reduced expression of lineage markers.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is necessary for HSPC induction.
source: These loss-of-function studies show that dnmt3bb.1 is necessary for HSPC induction; additional gain-of–function experiments we performed show that dnmt3bb.1 is also sufficient to drive hematopoietic development.
evidence: This claim is supported by loss-of-function experimental data.

claim: dnmt3bb.1 is sufficient to drive hematopoietic development.
source: These loss-of-function studies show that dnmt3bb.1 is necessary for HSPC induction; additional gain-of–function experiments we performed show that dnmt3bb.1 is also sufficient to drive hematopoietic development.
evidence: This claim is supported by gain-of-function experimental data.

claim: Ectopic mosaic overexpression of Dnmt3bb.1 activates hematopoietic gene expression in non-hemogenic endothelium.
source: Ectopic mosaic overexpression of Dnmt3bb.1 activates hematopoietic gene expression in non-hemogenic endothelium, and even in 'naive' cells in the early blastula well before normal emergence of HSPC or specification of any blood cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data from transgene overexpression experiments.

claim: Ectopic mosaic overexpression of Dnmt3bb.1 activates hematopoietic gene expression in 'naive' cells in the early blastula well before normal emergence of HSPC or specification of any blood cell lineages.
source: Ectopic mosaic overexpression of Dnmt3bb.1 activates hematopoietic gene expression in non-hemogenic endothelium, and even in 'naive' cells in the early blastula well before normal emergence of HSPC or specification of any blood cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data from transgene overexpression experiments in early blastulae.

claim: cd41:gfp transgene-positive HSPC isolated from transgenic zebrafish larvae populate the thymus upon transplantation.
source: Previous studies have shown that cd41:gfp transgene-positive HSPC isolated from transgenic zebrafish larvae populate the thymus upon transplantation (Bertrand et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Bertrand et al., 2008.

claim: Transplanted cells from dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastulae preferentially 'home' to the thymus and to the kidney.
source: Transplanted cells from dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastulae also preferentally 'home' to the thymus and to the kidney (data not shown), suggesting that these dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing cells are recapitulating at least one functional property of HSPCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by transplantation experiment data.

claim: dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing cells are recapitulating at least one functional property of HSPCs.
source: Transplanted cells from dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastulae also preferentally 'home' to the thymus and to the kidney (data not shown), suggesting that these dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing cells are recapitulating at least one functional property of HSPCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing cells home to the thymus like HSPCs.

claim: The remarkable capacity of dnmt3bb.1 to activate hematopoietic gene expression in non-hematopoietic cells appears to reflect a fairly direct conversion towards the hematopoietic lineage rather than a more general induction of mesoderm or hemogenic endothelium.
source: The remarkable capacity of dnmt3bb.1 to activate hematopoietic gene expression in non-hematopoietic cells appears to reflect a fairly direct conversion towards the hematopoietic lineage rather than a more general induction of mesoderm or hemogenic endothelium, since we do not observe ectopic expression of endothelial markers in dnmt3bb.1-overexpressing blastulae, nor do we detect ectopic expression of other markers of mesoderm (unpublished results).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that dnmt3bb.1 overexpression induces hematopoietic but not endothelial markers.

claim: The histone demethylase Kdm2b was shown to be able to promote the conversion of fibroblasts into iPS cells on its own.
source: Another epigenetic factor, the histone demethylase Kdm2b, was recently shown to be able to promote the conversion of fibroblasts into iPS cells on its own (Liang et al., 2012), reinforcing the idea that epigenetic factors can facilitate reprogramming independent of key specification factors (such as Oct4, Klf2 and Sox2 during iPS conversion).
evidence: This claim is supported by the citation to Liang et al., 2012.

claim: Epigenetic factors can facilitate reprogramming independent of key specification factors.
source: Another epigenetic factor, the histone demethylase Kdm2b, was recently shown to be able to promote the conversion of fibroblasts into iPS cells on its own (Liang et al., 2012), reinforcing the idea that epigenetic factors can facilitate reprogramming independent of key specification factors (such as Oct4, Klf2 and Sox2 during iPS conversion).
evidence: This is an inference based on the Kdm2b example and the dnmt3bb.1 results.

claim: Dnmt3bb.1 exerts its hematopoietic effects via Cmyb.
source: Our results strongly suggest that Dnmt3bb.1 exerts its hematopoietic effects via Cmyb.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Combined whole-genome analysis of gene expression and DNA methylation in HSPC isolated from double-transgenic zebrafish embryos by flow cytometry shows that cmyb is one of the most significant genes with both reduced expression and reduced DNA methylation in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC.
source: Combined whole-genome analysis of gene expression and DNA methylation in HSPC isolated from double-transgenic zebrafish embryos by flow cytometry shows that cmyb is one of the most significant genes with both reduced expression and reduced DNA methylation in dnmt3bb.1-deficient HSPC.
